WEDNESDAY, THE TWENTY FIFTH DAY OF MARCH, TWO THOUSAND NINE.

Oral Order : (Per Sri Syed Abdullah , Honble Member) ****   This complaint is filed attributing deficiency in service, unfair trade practice against the opposite parties 1 and 2 in respect of sale and supply of I Lab Digital Minilab along with Densito Meter and software and another one by name Pakon Film Scanner FS 235 plus as per the quotation dt.

12.1.2004 worth Rs.18,65,781/- and Rs.4,18,379/- which was found to be defective, second hand and that opposite parties 3 to 5 while advancing loan on hypothecation of said equipment had colluded with the opposite parties 1 and 2 on forged invoice as if it is a brand new one and thereby sought for the following reliefs.

1. to direct the opp.parties 1 and 2 to refund entire amount of Rs.16,95,989/- in respect of the equipment sold and supplied with interest thereon at 24% p.a. with quarterly rests till realization and consequently a. to award Rs.5,00,918/-

representing the monthly instalment of the loan amount so far paid by the complainant to the opp.parties 3 to 5 with interest @ 24% p.a. and future amounts payable, b.

to award interest to the tune of Rs.13,92,124/- representing the balance amount to be paid to the opp.parties 3 to 5 with interest at 24% p.a. c.

to award compensation to the tune of Rs.20 lakhs for the mental agony suffered

5. to direct the opp.parties 3 to 5 to pay to the complainant by way of damages and compensation to the tune of Rs.10 lakhs for collusion with the opp.party nos. 1 and 2 .

6. to direct the opp.parties 3 to 5 not to present the post dated cheques taken from the complainant for encashment and

7. to award punitive damages quantified at Rs.20 lakhs   Briefly stated facts as set out in the complaint are that under self employment the complainant as a proprietor of the firm Sri Jyothi Colour Lab situate at Ameerpet , Hyderabad had started Photo Colour Lab . In connection of professional work of the photo studio the complainant required Digital Minilab along with Densito Meter, its software along with Pakon Film Scanner FS 235 . So as to purchase the same, the complainant was in search of it and came across with news items and brochures. The opposite parties 1 and 2 conducted Photo Air Exhibition in the year 2004 at Mumbai where the complainant visited and sought displaying of the equipments and examined the same and he was appraised that the said equipments are brand new and imported one. The complainant was satisfied with the equipments and requested the opp.parties to supply the same for which they agreed and promised to supply it. A letter dt. 12.1.2004 was sent by the opposite party no.1 thanking for placing order and its representative was sent to the complainants place to display the equipment and represented that the equipments are best available in the market. A quotation was given on 12.1.2004 for an amount of Rs.18,65,781/- for one equipment and another equipment for an amount of Rs.4,18,379/- . On the inducement of the opposite parties 1 and 2 the complainant had approached the opposite party no.5 i.e ICICI Bank for loan facility and the bank had agreed to advance loan to a tune of Rs.17,13,120/- and that he agreed to take loan of Rs.11,95,989/- and Rs.5,00,000/- to purchase the equipments. The opposite parties 3 to5 sanctioned the loan. The said loan amount was given to opposite party no.1 by a cheque bearing no.

187875 dt. 17.3.2004 for Rs.5 lakhs and another DD bearing no.21956 dt. 17.3.2004 for Rs.11,95,989/- . Ever since the sanction of loan, the complainant began to pay monthly instalments at Rs.45,538/- i.e. from 22.4.2004 and paid instalments upto 22.2.2005 . The equipments were delivered after lot of persuasion . However the equipments never worked from the date of installation. A protest was made with the opposite parties for their mis-representation that the equipments supplied are new one for which they agreed to replace with new equipment . A letter dt. 18.4.2005 was addressed in this regard. The opposite parties 1 and 2 did not replace the equipment . So the complainant went to Mumbai on 22.6.2005 . He also visited the Head Quarters of ICICI Bank where he found that the opposite party no.1 in collusion with the bank authorities i.e. opposite parties 3 to 5 had directly submitted the invoice to the bank at Mumbai in which it is mentioned that brand new equipment was supplied. The invoice ought to have been sent to the complainant . There was fraudulent motive on the part of the opposite parties. Since the opposite parties 1 and 2 have not replaced the brand new equipment, a legal notice dt. 15.9.2005 was sent to the opposite parties. The opposite parties have committed illegalities as well deficiency in service. The complainant had suffered a loss to a tune of Rs.90 lakhs . Hence the complaint.

 

The opposite parties 1 and 2 filed their version and opposite party no.5 filed separate version. Interalia the version is as under:

They took a stand that the complaint is not maintainable and complainant is not a consumer and goods are purchased for commercial purpose and the complainant is having other allied business interests. The opposite parties 1 and 2 have supplied the machine and its equipment in a workable condition which was inspected and approved by the complainant when he visited the works of the opp.parties. The opposite parties sent a reply dt. 21.3.2005 to the complainant explaining the reasons behind the difficulties in operating the machine and pointing out that the complainant should be well conversant with not only operation but also maintenance and trouble shooting of the equipment by taking extensive training on LPDM . The machine was installed in April 2004 itself . Idleness of the machinery as alleged was not due to any defect but due to lack of operational skills by the complainant or his employees.

A concoction was made stating that it was a defective one and there are contradictions in his legal notice and in the complaint. The opposite parties 1 and 2 strongly suspect that the complainant wants to avoid payment of loan instalments with the bank and had made allegations that defective equipment was supplied . False allegation is made that invoice was forged.

 

The opp.party no.5 stated that the complainant has availed a loan of Rs.11,95,989/- and Rs.5 lakhs by entering into an agreement and agreeing to repay the same in monthly instalments @ Rs.45,538/- for a period of 48 months and pursuant there to, he started paying instalments from 22.4.2004 till 22.2.2005 and thereafter defaulted in payment of instalments.. It is false to allege that the invoice was obtained directly from the opposite party no.1 , neither the complainant nor the opposite party no. 1 delivered any invoice. In order to avoid loan repayment the complainant set up false allegations. Infact the complainant violated terms and conditions of the loan agreement by making false allegations of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice which is attributed towards the corporate bank without any bonafides. Hence prayed to dismiss the complaint.

 

The points that arise for consideration are Whether the opp.parties 1 and 2 have sold and supplied defective second hand equipment to the complainant other than agreed to be sold as alleged by the complainant? Whether the opp.parties 3 to 5 in collusion with opposite parties 1 and 2 basing on forged invoice have sanctioned the loan ? Whether the complainant is entitled for refund of Rs.16,95,989/- with interest there on being the total value paid by him? Whether the complainant is entitled for the reliefs claimed against the opp.parties 3 to 5? Whether the complainant had purchased the equipment for commercial purpose which bars him to invoke the jurisdiction of Consumer Protection Act?

The complainant as well the opposite parties filed documents along with evidence affidavits which are marked as Exs.A1 to A 13 and Exs.B1 to B9 Point no.1:The undisputed facts are that the opposite parties 1 and 2 have sold and supplied photo equipment in question and the opposite parties 3 to 5 have sanctioned loan on the basis of loan agreement. Initially the burden of proof is on the complainant to establish that the machinery or photo equipment in question which was purchased or sold and supplied by the opp.parties 1 and 2 is either defective, mis branded or second hand as alleged by him in the complaint , so also to establish that there is deficiency in service as well that unfair trade practice was adopted in sale of the equipment, as defined under Section2(1)(f) and (g) that the goods are faulty lacking perfection or shortcoming in quality or standard which is required to be maintained as required under law or as per contract. The evidence placed by the complainant is to be looked into to find out whether the photo equipments in question are defective one as alleged. Ex.A1 is a loan cum hypothecation agreement dt. 18.12.2005 signed by the complainant as proprietor of Jyothi Color Lab in which terms and conditions are incorporated . The terms of the agreement binds by both parties i.e. the complainant and opposite parties 3 to 5. Before entering into agreement the bank had issued a letter to the complainant requiring him to fulfill its conditions . On fulfilling the conditions the loan was sanctioned and there is no dispute in this regard. Ex.A2 is the letter dt. 12.1.2004 issued by the opposite parties 1 and 2 in the name of the complainant informing that quotations who sent to him and that demonstration of product was already made to him by the marketing team to satisfy him about the product.

Ex.A3 and A4 are the quotations dt. 12.1.2004 issued by the opp.parties 1 and 2 issued for a sum of Rs.4,18,379/- and Rs.18,65,781/- Ex.A5 is a receipt dt. 12.1.2004 passed by the opp.parties for a sum of Rs.5 lakhs received from the complainant . Similarly Ex.A6 is copies of cheques issued by ICICI bank in favour of the opp.parties 1 and 2 in token of payment of Rs.5 lakhs and Rs.11,95,989/- paid towards the cost of the equipments . It is clear that by means of a Memorandum of Understanding in between the complainant and opp.parties 1 and 2 along with others a service contract was entered for repair and maintenance . Ex.A7 is the copy of cheque for Rs.11,95,989/- .One of the condition in Ex.A8 states that Installation and service will be provided promptly by AGILE as and when the equipment fails and the equipment will be under warranty and service for two years . For CPDM one years for machine. The opposite party also promised to depute their service engineer within 48 hours in case of failure of equipment . Ex.A9 is the copy of repayment schedule . Ex.A10 is the notice dt. 18.4.2005 sent by the complainant to the opp.party no.1 . Ex.A11 is the copy of the bank statement which shows that the payments and the banking transactions in respect of payment of E.M.I. during the period from 14.1.2004 to 22.2.2004 . Ex.A12 and A13 are the copies of the legal notice issued by the complainant to the opp.parties . None of these documents would establish that the equipments in question are either defective or second hand or mis branded and on the contra the opposite parties 1 and 2 have filed Exs.B1 to B9 . Ex.B1 is affidavit given by Service Engineer of M/s. PAgile Phototechnicks Pvt Ltd . certifying that I-Lab is an assembled machine in India ,M/s. Agile Phtotechnicks imports the new digital engine and electronics from M/s.Labnet Plus of Poland, and they fix the same on a Noritsu 1501 machine. Agile uses the processor section and body of the Noritsu 1501 machine, and the contact printing unit and other associated electronics imported from Labnet plus is fitted in the machine to make the new digital machine I-Lab. He further certified that it was a very good machine available in the market at that time , at the quoted cost and quality , other new digital machines available at that time were costing more than 25-30 lakhs rupees. Further I-Lab is a fully computerized digital machine and highly skilled person is required to operate the same . One need to have extensive hands on training on the I-Lab , daily calibration and set up of the machine requires thorough computer knowledge and then only one will be able to run the digital machine (1-Lab) to produce good quality prints. He further stated that the equipment supplied to the complainant was personally checked by him and conducted necessary burn out tests and he was found out satisfactory without any operational problems and that operation was demonstrated to the complainant and after proper testing and demonstration the machinery was supplied to the entire satisfaction of the complainant. Ex.B2 is the warranty dt. 8.4.2004 stating that the equipment I-Lab Digital Minilab with Densitometer Film Scanner F 335 Plus & Software is having 6 months warrantee from the date of delivery for any manufacturing defects . Ex.B3 is affidavit given by Proprietor of M/s.Super Color Lab Company . Ex.B4 is the certificate issued by Panorama Digital Imaging Technology certifying that a digital mini lab I-Lab purchased from opposite party no.1 during the year 2004 as of best quality and with good purpose . Similarly Ex.B5 is also a certificate issued by Chopra Digital Color Photo Lab . Ex.B6 is copy of Minutes of Meeting signed by complainant and opp.parties along with service engineer. Ex.B7 is the letter dt.31.3.2005 from the complainant to opp.party no.2 requesting to exchange the machine as promised . Ex.B8 is letter dt.

12.4.2005 from the opp.party no.2 to the complainant stating that they have made more than 10 service visits to the complainants lab in one year and at no stage during their deal or discussion they promised to exchange the machine . In the said letter opp.party requested the complainant to inform their willingness to take exclusive training on the machine.. Ex.B9 is the Legal notice dt. 15.10.2005 issued by the complainant to the opp.parties 1 & 2.

 

Point no.1:The complainant has not filed any rejoinder to the facts stated by the Service Engineer or other customers who said to have purchased I Lab Photo Equipments and other equipments from opp.parties 1 and 2 No steps were taken to cross examine them or file interrogatories . So it can be said that these documents Exs.B1 to B9 remained unchallenged. Whenever a complaint is filed alleging defect in the goods it cannot be determined without proper analysis or test of the goods. The complainant has to invoke the procedure as contemplated under Section 13(1) for sending it to proper lab to determine its functioning and quality. It is not known why the complainant has not taken any such steps atleast after filing of the complaint or during the pendency of the case especially when the complainant has made allegations that the opposite parties 1 and 2 by playing fraud have sold and supplied a second hand machinery and on their inducement the ICICI Bank had sanctioned loan and the said amount was drawn by them . Except allegations no evidence worth enough is placed and on the other hand the evidence of opposite parties 1 and 2 would establish that the equipment was supplied as per its quotations and specifications. So point no.1 is held against the complainant and in favour of the opposite parties 1 and 2 .

 

Point nos.2 to 4:

With regard to the allegations that the opposite parties 1 and 2 in collusion with opposite parties 3 to 5 have directly sent the invoice to see that the loan is disbursed and payment is received from the bank which is neither proved nor established by any cogent and satisfactory evidence . After all the opposite parties 3 to 5 have been doing banking business who are carrying on their business by following banking guidelines for disbursement of loan which they cannot apply differently to different customers. The documents maintained by bank are relevant and acceptable evidence and in case any fraud or forgery was played it is for the loanee to explain it. Ex.A8/B6 Memorandum of Understanding was entered on 7.4.2004 which was subsequent to entering into loan cum hypothecation agreement and payments of amounts covered by the quotations. The payment was made to the opposite parties 1 and 2 in January and thereafter Memorandum of Understanding was entered for the maintenance and warranty with regard to the equipment that was sold. Atleast soon after entering Memorandum of Understanding , the complainant would have addressed a letter to the opposite parties 1 and 2 about the alleged defects , but he did not do so. For the first time on 18.4.2005 he addressed a letter to the opposite party no.1 which is exactly one year thereafter.
The complainant failed to show on what he received the equipment and within the warranty period itself it became non- functional. There is no evidence on record to accept his version that the equipment was supplied belatedly and thereby he could not know the defects until he started operating it. Though the pleadings are drafted with legal acumen to bring the case within the fold of the deficiency in service and unfair trade practice but the evidence on record is completely vague and hollow. So this point is held against the complainant.
Point no.5: Even if any goods are purchased for commercial purpose , the purchaser will be a Consumer within the meaning of Section 2(d) of Consumer Protection Act and in case the goods purchased or sold are defective the aggrieved may see the dealer and manufacturer for replacement a compensation provided the case is filed within the warranty period and proving it by showing experts evidence about its defects.
 
On an overall consideration of factual aspects , the evidence on record in the back ground of the statutory provisions it can be said without any hesitation that the complainant miserably failed to establish that the opposite parties 1 and 2 have sold and supplied defective or second hand machine ( photo equipments) to attract the definitions of defect and deficiency in service so also unfair trade practice as per Section2(f)(g) and of the Consumer Protection Act.
 

In the result the complaint is dismissed with costs of Rs.5000/- payable to the opp.parties 1 &2 and 3 to 5 separately.
